name: Virginia DVS free accredited claims assistance
description: Free state help with disability claims, pension benefits, appeals and survivor-related benefits.
next_step: Use the official Disability Claims, Pensions & Appeals page to choose the relevant service. Request an appointment with a DVS representative through Book a Disability Claims Appointment, or call 844-838-7838 for office routing if the form does not load. Ask what records to bring and whether remote assistance is available.
constraints: The published phone is the statewide DVS routing number, not a guaranteed direct line to a claims specialist.

The online appointment form remained at Loading services during this review. Use the phone fallback if you encounter the same problem; this observation does not establish that the form is unavailable to everyone.
A referral does not establish benefit eligibility. Work with an appropriately accredited representative on claims and appeals.

evidence.selection: Read full rendered official DVS program and Claims Basics pages. The statewide phone is published in the DVS footer. Inspected the appointment form without entering data or submitting it.

name: Virginia state veterans care centers
description: State veterans homes offer skilled nursing, rehabilitation and memory-care services.
next_step: Open the official care-center page and choose Roanoke, Virginia Beach, Richmond or Fauquier. Use that center’s Eligibility Application link or Request Assistance from DVS for Care Center. If a form or download does not open, call 844-838-7838 and ask for the selected center’s admissions contact.
constraints: The phone is statewide DVS referral routing; ask for the selected care center’s admissions team. It is not a direct admissions line.

Ask the admissions team to review military service, residency, clinical care needs and payment. The official page has additional service-duration and Guard/Reserve criteria. Do not assume eligibility, a bed or funding.

Application links are published on the full official page. Downloads hosted on the legacy DVS domain could not be checked because that domain returns access-denied errors. Use the assistance-request or phone fallback if a link fails.

evidence.selection: Read the complete rendered official care-center page, including all four center sections, admissions criteria, application links and statewide DVS footer contact. No application submitted.

name: Virginia Easy Access / No Wrong Door
organization: Virginia Department for Aging and Rehabilitative Services
description: State navigation tool for older adults, people with disabilities, veterans and caregivers seeking community support.
next_step: Call the published navigation line or use Service Finder. Give your county or independent city and describe the service you need.
constraints: Confirm the service requirements, intake arrangements and availability with the agency.

name: Virginia local Area Agencies on Aging
organization: Virginia Department for Aging and Rehabilitative Services
description: The state directory matches each county and independent city to an Area Agency on Aging.
next_step: Choose your county or independent city in the official directory and call the listed agency. Ask for information and assistance, a needs assessment and local support options.
constraints: Use the county-matched agency phone in the directory; this is a directory rather than one statewide intake office.
Distinguish independent cities from same-named counties.

name: VICAP free Medicare counseling
organization: Virginia Department for Aging and Rehabilitative Services
description: Free, unbiased Medicare counseling through local aging agencies.
next_step: Contact the Area Agency on Aging for your county or independent city and ask to schedule a VICAP counseling session. Ask about plan choices, costs, assistance programs, appeals or coverage denials.
constraints: The official page directs appointments exclusively through local aging agencies; use the county-matched contact.
Counselors explain options and do not sell insurance.

name: Virginia CCC Plus Medicaid waiver screening
organization: Virginia Department of Medical Assistance Services
description: Medicaid home and community-based services screening for older adults and people with physical disabilities or ongoing skilled nursing needs.
next_step: Request an LTSS screening through your local department of social services. If hospitalized, ask the discharge planner. Apply for Medicaid separately through CommonHelp, Cover Virginia or local social services; request Appendix D for a paper LTSS application.
constraints: The phone is the Cover Virginia Medicaid application line, not a substitute for the local LTSS screening team.
Medicaid financial eligibility and LTSS screening are separate requirements. Ask the screening team about providers after approval.
For home adaptations, members in managed care should contact their MCO care coordinator; fee-for-service members should use the DMAS member guide. Obtain written authorization before work.

name: Virginia State Long-Term Care Ombudsman
organization: Virginia Department for Aging and Rehabilitative Services
description: State and local advocates help address long-term-care service and resident-rights concerns.
next_step: Use the local ombudsman directory or call the published state-office number. Explain the care concern and give the facility location or home-care service area.
constraints: Confirm the service requirements, intake arrangements and availability with the agency.

name: Virginia family caregiver support
organization: Virginia Department for Aging and Rehabilitative Services
description: Caregiver information, support and respite navigation through local aging agencies.
next_step: Call your county-matched aging agency. Ask about caregiver information, support groups, training, respite and the assessment or application needed for each service.
constraints: Services and respite options have their own requirements; ask the local agency what is available.
This page does not publish a single statewide caregiver intake number.

name: Virginia Assistive Technology System
organization: Virginia Department for Aging and Rehabilitative Services
description: Assistive technology consultations, demonstrations, short-term loans and equipment-resource navigation.
next_step: Call to explain the task that is difficult and ask about a consultation, device demonstration, loan or available reused equipment. Ask which local program can handle a durable medical equipment request.
constraints: The program states it does not have funds to buy assistive technology for individuals.
Equipment availability and suitability must be confirmed. This is not a promise of free equipment or construction funding.

name: disAbility Law Center of Virginia
description: Disability rights advocacy and information from Virginia’s protection and advocacy organization.
next_step: Read the current goals and issue exclusions on Get Help, then choose either the online request form or phone intake at 800-552-3962. Describe the disability-rights problem and any deadline. Do not submit a form and call about the same issue, and do not send service requests to the general information email address.
constraints: Assistance must fit the organization’s current goals and focus areas; requesting help does not create an attorney-client relationship or guarantee representation.
The intake page excludes direct financial aid, initial Social Security applications, criminal representation and several other matters; review the full exclusion list before applying.
Intake is free. Use one request method. You remain responsible for your deadlines.

evidence.selection: Reviewed the full official Get Help page through web retrieval: intake methods, main phone, no-email instruction, scope/exclusions, no-duplicate-request instruction and representation disclaimer. Direct local HTTP retrieval still failed, but full official page text was available through web retrieval.

name: Virginia blind and vision-impaired services
organization: Virginia Department for the Blind and Vision Impaired
description: Specialized services for blind, vision-impaired and deafblind Virginians, including independent living and orientation and mobility.
next_step: Call or use the official Apply for Services route. Ask for the regional office and an assessment for low-vision, orientation and mobility, rehabilitation teaching or independent-living needs.
constraints: Confirm the service requirements, intake arrangements and availability with the agency.

name: Virginia Relay
organization: Virginia Department for the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
description: Telephone relay for deaf, hard-of-hearing, deafblind and speech-disabled people communicating with telephone users.
next_step: Dial 711 for a relay call. For equipment or communication support beyond relay, use the department’s equipment and community-service links.
constraints: Confirm the service requirements, intake arrangements and availability with the agency.

name: Virginia 211 community support
description: State-designated information and referral route for housing, food and other community services.
next_step: Dial 211 and give your county or independent city. Ask for current local housing, shelter, food, transportation or emergency-assistance intake contacts.
constraints: Confirm the service requirements, intake arrangements and availability with the agency.
